theme: Time-series datasets curated for tourism forecasting research (Monash, M-competitions tourism, Kaggle tourism forecasting), tourism demand models with data

gh search repos "monash forecasting" --sort stars (0 results)
gh search repos "monash time series repository" --sort stars (0 results)
gh search repos "M4 competition tourism" --sort stars (0 results)
gh search repos "Rob Hyndman tourism" --sort stars (0 results)
WebFetch raw READMEs: ellisp/Tcomp-r-package, Affan-M/TourismForecastReconciliation, zhiqin1998/tourism-forecasting (404), Roberto-Perrotta/Turismo_Salento_forecasting

candidates.name: Tcomp-r-package
candidates.what_it_holds: R package mirroring the classic 2010/2011 Tourism Forecasting Competition dataset (Athanasopoulos et al. 2011), sourced originally from Rob Hyndman's site. 1,311 tourism time series (yearly/quarterly/monthly, `Mdata` objects, same class structure as the Mcomp M-competition packages) submitted by tourism organisations and academics worldwide. Data lives inside the package (list object `tourism`), prep scripts in /prep/.
candidates.why_useful: This is the canonical academic tourism-forecasting benchmark dataset (real submitted tourism arrivals/demand series across many countries) — directly answers the theme's core ask. Useful less as an ABNB predictor and more as a methods testbed: it is the standard corpus for validating hierarchical/reconciliation and ensemble forecasting techniques (gap 17, methods) that the team could apply to nights/ADR quarterly forecasting.
candidates.geography: Global (many countries, unspecified per-series in metadata)
candidates.time_coverage: Pre-2010 tourism series (submitted for the 2010 competition), multiple frequencies
candidates.size_hint: 1,311 series, small (R package, likely a few MB)

candidates.name: M4-methods
candidates.what_it_holds: Official M4 forecasting competition data and benchmark methods, ~100,000 time series across 6 frequencies (yearly/quarterly/monthly/weekly/daily/hourly) and multiple domains including a 'Tourism' domain (a large subset of quarterly/monthly/yearly tourism-related series, distinct from and larger than the smaller Tcomp 2010 set). Full train/test CSVs plus R/Python benchmark implementations (naive, ETS, ARIMA, Theta, ML hybrids).
candidates.why_useful: The Tourism-domain subset of M4 is a large, real, multi-frequency tourism time-series corpus usable for validating forecasting methodology (seasonal decomposition, reconciliation, ensembling) before applying to ABNB KPIs; also the general M4 corpus is the standard cross-domain forecasting-method benchmark referenced in the industry.
candidates.time_coverage: Series lengths vary by frequency; competition run 2018
candidates.size_hint: ~100k series total, Tourism subset a few thousand; full repo is tens of MB
candidates.last_activity: active org, exact date not checked

candidates.name: M5-methods
candidates.what_it_holds: Official M5 competition (Walmart retail sales) data and benchmark methods notebooks.
candidates.why_useful: Not tourism-specific (retail, not travel) but same forecasting-competition family and reconciliation methodology used for hierarchical demand forecasting — marginal use as a methods reference only.

candidates.name: M6-methods
candidates.what_it_holds: Official M6 competition data/methods for financial forecasting (stock and portfolio return prediction), not tourism.
candidates.why_useful: Off-theme (financial markets, not travel demand) but flagged for completeness since it is the third M-competition repo; essentially no tourism relevance.

candidates.name: TourismForecastReconciliation
candidates.what_it_holds: R project producing short-term tourism forecasts (ARIMA, ETS, dynamic harmonic regression, forecast reconciliation) for the Maldives, pulling directly from the Maldives Monetary Authority's public query database API (https://database.mma.gov.mv/api). Needs a user-supplied API key stored in a local Secrets.R file; no bulk data committed.
candidates.why_useful: A working, scriptable client for a national-authority tourism/monetary database (APAC/Indian Ocean tourism-dependent economy) — relevant to gap 7 (regional travel volume outside US/EU) as a template for pulling government tourism series, and gap 17 for reconciliation methodology, though the underlying data itself is Maldives-specific and probably too small a market to move ABNB directly.
candidates.time_coverage: Whatever MMA's API exposes (not stated precisely)

candidates.name: Turismo_Salento_forecasting
candidates.what_it_holds: Istat (Italian national statistics institute) 'movimento clienti esercizi ricettivi' (guest movement in accommodation establishments) for Lecce province / Salento region, 92 municipalities, annual, 2014-2024, extracted from 11 annual worksheets into a committed processed file `lecce_turismo_pulito.csv` (760 rows x 27 columns). Also cross-references 9,752 Inside Airbnb Naples listings (Sept 2025 snapshot) as a South-Italy STR pricing proxy, and runs Facebook Prophet forecasts.
candidates.why_useful: A committed, cleaned Italian municipal-level tourism accommodation panel (2014-2024) — a finer-grained, longer regional hotel/accommodation demand series than what we currently hold for Southern Italy, and a second independent Inside-Airbnb Naples pull that could be checked against our own IA captures for basis consistency.
candidates.size_hint: 760 rows x 27 cols processed CSV + Istat source worksheets referenced

candidates.name: Tourism-forecasting-
candidates.what_it_holds: Described as using 'actual Sri Lankan tourism data (2014-2025)' with ARIMA seasonality modelling; student project, data provenance (likely Sri Lanka Tourism Development Authority) not independently verified.
candidates.why_useful: A recent (through 2025) national tourist-arrivals series for an APAC tourism-dependent market not otherwise covered; low confidence the repo has more than a small CSV, but fills gap 7 partially if genuine.

candidates.name: Kenya-tourism-forecasting
candidates.what_it_holds: Comparison of ARIMA, SARIMA, Prophet and Holt-Winters on international tourist arrivals to Kenya; presumably a small committed arrivals CSV (likely sourced from Kenya national bureau of statistics or UNWTO), not verified in detail.
candidates.why_useful: Africa is essentially absent from our current regional-volume holdings; if the underlying arrivals series is genuine it is a rare African tourism time series on GitHub.

candidates.name: UK-Tourism-Forecasting-AI-Prophet
candidates.what_it_holds: Facebook Prophet model forecasting yearly UK tourist arrivals using 'real Kaggle data' (likely ONS/VisitBritain international-visitor series repackaged on Kaggle).
candidates.why_useful: A UK arrivals series is adjacent to our existing Eurostat/EU coverage; only worth a look if the Kaggle source file is actually committed rather than downloaded at runtime (not verified).
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: partial overlap with existing Eurostat/EU tourism coverage

candidates.name: tourism-forecasting (Zermatt)
candidates.what_it_holds: 'Zermatt Tourism Demand Forecaster' — time-series analysis for Alpine tourism (Switzerland), 96 months of data including a COVID-impact period, delivered as a Streamlit app.
candidates.why_useful: Niche single-destination (Zermatt, Swiss Alps) monthly tourism series with explicit COVID break marked — potentially useful as a small case study of demand-shock recovery patterns analogous to travel-shock scenarios (gap 11), but very narrow geography.

candidates.name: PH_Tourism_Deep_Learning
candidates.what_it_holds: Data and R scripts for 'Tourism Demand Forecasting in the Philippines Using Deep Learning Models' — an academic-style replication package for a Philippines tourist-arrivals forecasting study.
candidates.why_useful: APAC market (Philippines) tourist-arrivals series not currently in our holdings, packaged as an academic replication set (data + code), which fits the 'academic replication package' category explicitly called out as in-scope.

candidates.name: Code_-secondary-decomposition
candidates.what_it_holds: Code for 'a new secondary decomposition ensemble approach for tourism demand forecasting' (academic paper replication); likely includes the paper's tourist-arrivals dataset (probably Chinese destination, not confirmed) alongside decomposition-ensemble forecasting code (e.g. CEEMDAN + ML).
candidates.why_useful: A decomposition-ensemble method specifically built for tourism demand series — could be tested against our own nights/ADR series as an alternative to the ETS/ARIMA baselines already tried and found wanting; data provenance unconfirmed so flagged as method more than dataset.

candidates.name: tourism-forecasting (post-pandemic ensemble RNN)
candidates.what_it_holds: Code repository accompanying 'Post-pandemic tourism forecasting with ensemble RNN' published in Annals of Tourism Research. README fetch 404'd (branch/path mismatch), so contents not directly confirmed in this pass — likely contains a published paper's tourism dataset plus RNN ensemble code given the paper citation in the repo description.
candidates.why_useful: A peer-reviewed academic replication package explicitly targeting COVID/post-pandemic tourism demand recovery patterns (relevant to gap 11 shock modelling and gap 17 methods) — worth a follow-up repo browse by whichever agent picks this up, since the description is credible even though the README fetch failed.

candidates.name: aws-thailand-tourism-demand-forecast
candidates.what_it_holds: 'ML.FORECAST predicts arrivals from 20 source markets' for Thailand tourism, framed as an AWS/Snowflake demo (enabling capacity planning, marketing spend allocation). Likely a vendor demo notebook with sample or synthetic data rather than a real bulk Thailand tourism-authority dataset; not independently verified.
candidates.why_useful: If the underlying arrivals-by-source-market data is real (rather than synthetic demo data), Thailand is a significant APAC tourism market and source-market breakdowns would be a genuinely new granularity (gap 7); flagged low-confidence pending verification.

notes: gh search repos for tourism-forecasting-specific terms surfaced almost entirely student/bootcamp ML projects (many near-identical Sri Lanka/India tourism-demand-forecasting titles from the same course cohorts) rather than curated research datasets; the genuinely notable finds came from knowing the M-competition/Hyndman lineage by name (Tcomp-r-package, Mcompetitions org) rather than from keyword search. 'monash forecasting', 'monash time series repository', 'M4 competition tourism', and 'Rob Hyndman tourism' all returned zero gh search results (gh search repos does not index README/description text well for these compound terms) — the actual Monash Time Series Forecasting Repository (forecastingdata.org / Godahewa et al. LibForecast) lives primarily off-GitHub or under names not tried here (e.g. an actual 'monash-forecasting-repository' GitHub org/repo was not confirmed to exist under gh search and was not found before the search budget ran out); a future scout with WebSearch budget available should check for a GitHub mirror of that repository specifically, since it is the most likely single highest-value miss for this theme. Two of six allotted gh search calls returned zero and two WebSearch calls failed because the session's shared web-search budget (200/200) was already exhausted before this scout ran, which also blocked broader keyword sweeps (Kaggle tourism forecasting github, tourism demand model with data, etc.) — those keyword angles are unexplored and worth another scout's pass. WebFetch on github.com/search (the web search-repos UI page) hit a 429 rate limit; direct org/user page and raw README fetches worked fine and are the more reliable pattern under the CDN allowlist constraints anyway.
